title: Chinese to Pinyin Converter: Tone Marks, Initials, and Readings
description: Convert Chinese to pinyin with tone marks, without tones, or as initials. Compare separators and verify readings, punctuation, line breaks, and empty input.
content:
Open the Chinese to Pinyin Converter, paste Chinese characters into the Input Chinese box, choose an output mode and separator, then click Convert. Use tone marks to verify pronunciation, or use unmarked pinyin or initials for indexing. Review the text in Conversion Result, then click Copy.

Try the converter with Hànyǔ pīnyīn

Enter 「汉语拼音」 and select Full pinyin (with tones) and Space. Click Convert. The result should be "hàn yǔ pīn yīn", and the status should read "Conversion complete". Match the four syllables to the source characters to see whether the clipboard included a heading or other stray text.

The defaults are Full pinyin (with tones) and None for the separator. If you see "hànyǔpīnyīn", verify the separator setting, select Space, and click Convert again. Click Sample to fill the input box with the built-in example. Click Clear to start over. It clears the input and result and hides the status message.

Keep these settings when you first try your own text. Review the result from left to right against the source and note the characters in any unfamiliar proper names. Before pasting the draft into a document, switch to unmarked pinyin or initials if your task calls for it. This lets you verify pronunciation and output format separately.

Choose an output mode

The same Chinese text can produce pronunciation notes, easy-to-type lookup values, or short labels. The examples below all use Hànyǔ pīnyīn with Space as the separator. Switch only the output mode to see which tone marks and syllable letters each mode keeps.

Output modeConversion resultUse case
Full pinyin (with tones)hàn yǔ pīn yīnVerify pronunciation or prepare learning materials
Full pinyin (no tones)han yu pin yinCreate an easy-to-type lookup field
Initialsh y p yCreate short labels or a secondary index

Full pinyin without tones keeps the syllable letters. Try 「女」. With tones, the result is "nǚ". Without tones, it is "nü". If the destination accepts only English letters, verify its input rules with a sample like this and follow its conventions. Removing tone marks and transliterating letters are separate steps.

Use separators to preserve syllable boundaries

The separator options are None, Space, Hyphen, and Underscore. The page gets an array of pinyin segments and inserts the chosen separator between them, following JavaScript's array join behavior [S4]. Try 「西安」 in Full pinyin (no tones) with None and then with Hyphen.

None gives "xian", and Hyphen gives "xi-an". Use the first form when the destination expects a single joined value. The second makes it easier to match syllables to the source text. For a lookup value, you can review pronunciation with Space first, then convert again using the field's required separator. Separators control how segments are joined. Review formal spelling separately.

If another program will process the output, use a short sample to see whether the separator survives import. For a field that requires underscores, try 「西安」 and expect "xi_an". When you review the imported data, verify whether the table treated the separator as a column delimiter.

Use initials for short labels

Convert 「长大」 with Initials and Hyphen to get "z-d". Full pinyin with tones and spaces gives "zhǎng dà". The library defines an initial as the first character of the pinyin syllable [S1]. To keep a sequence such as "zh", start with full pinyin for further processing.

Initials collapse pronunciation differences. Convert 「是」 and 「四」 separately and both give "s". In a contact list or product table, keep the pinyin label next to the original name and use the label to filter entries. To find a particular record when labels match, use the original name or an existing ID.

Initials reduce typing in lookup fields but can return more matches. Keep a full pinyin column for more precise searches. When generating both columns for a name, use the same Chinese source for both. Update the corresponding pinyin whenever a name changes.

Enter the whole word for characters with multiple readings

To verify the pronunciation of 「行」, paste the word that contains it. With tone marks and spaces, 「银行」 gives "yín háng" and 「行走」 gives "xíng zǒu". If both words appear in the source, mark each one and compare it with the corresponding syllable in the output.

The pinyin-pro documentation distinguishes between the API that selects a reading from text and the API that lists possible readings for a single character [S2]. This page uses the context-based API. When verifying a surname in a list, keep the full name and ask the person if the pronunciation is unclear. Unicode's Unihan documentation also notes that a common-reading field can differ from a dictionary's preferred reading [S3].

Review punctuation and letters in mixed text

Convert 「上海A版，」 with Full pinyin (no tones) and Hyphen to get "shang-hai-A-ban-，". The output keeps the Latin letter and the Chinese comma. For a file name or import field, verify that the destination accepts the comma next to the hyphen.

If you copied the source from a table, try a short excerpt that contains spaces or line breaks. Enter 「上海」, then a line break, then 「北京」. With Hyphen selected, the result retains the line break with a hyphen on each side. You can use the Text Toolbox to try trimming whitespace at the start and end of lines. Keep a copy of the original Chinese text so you can verify record boundaries after cleanup.

If the source already contains a connector, compare the result with a different separator. Try 「甲-乙」 with Underscore to get "jia_-_yi". The middle hyphen comes from the source. Identify the characters that were already present before adapting the result to the target format. This helps preserve meaningful symbols during cleanup.

Prepare pinyin for your document

Keep the original Chinese and the derived pinyin as needed for your task. For side-by-side review, put the Chinese in one column and the pinyin with tone marks next to it. Review place names, personal names, and words with possible alternate readings first. For material others will read, verify the readings before adjusting spacing and capitalization by word.

To display pronunciation above Chinese characters on a web page, format the plain-text result first. HTML can use the ruby element to annotate the source text with its pronunciation [S6]. This tool provides pinyin text in the result box. For spreadsheet searches, put the text in a separate pinyin column so readers can still see the corresponding Chinese characters.

For learning materials, list unfamiliar words separately or mark the words you plan to cover in a sentence. Verify each word's pinyin before marking pauses. If the destination document has its own layout conventions, try a short sentence you have already reviewed and inspect the positions of the annotations and source characters.

Limits of the conversion

China's Ministry of Education states that Hanyu Pinyin uses Standard Mandarin as its pronunciation basis [S5]. For dialect pronunciations, customary name readings, or official place-name spellings, consult the references specified for your task. Treat each segment in the result as part of a draft for review and keep the source text so you can trace corrections.

Review rare characters individually. For example, enter 「𰻞」 and convert it. The output still shows the original character. If you need to identify a character that was left in the output, use the Unicode Converter to verify it. Copy the original character and look up its pronunciation in the reference for your task. Verify any similar-looking characters against the source as well.

Pinyin alone cannot uniquely identify the original text. 「张三」 and 「章三」 both give "zhāng sān" with Full pinyin (with tones) and Space. If you need to look up the Chinese later, store the original name and pinyin separately. Use the original names to distinguish records with the same pronunciation.

Start with a short word when testing Traditional Chinese. With tone marks and spaces, 「開發」 gives "kāi fā". Keep the original character forms during review and update the pinyin column according to the pronunciation. If the source uses different forms in different entries, you can still look up each record using its original spelling.

Status messages and what to verify before copying

If the input box is empty, clicking Convert displays "Please enter Chinese". If the result box already contains text, it keeps the previous result. When you see this message, reenter the source text, convert again, and wait for the status to update before copying. The tool still processes input that contains only spaces. If the input looks blank, clear it and enter the text again.

If the program catches a conversion exception, it displays "Conversion failed:" followed by the exception message. Try a short input such as Hànyǔ pīnyīn to see whether it also produces an error. The result box is read-only. To make corrections, copy the pinyin into your document and edit it against the original word.

Final review before delivery

Before copying, verify that the input box contains the original text you intend to use. For a batch, review an entry with a character that has multiple readings and an entry with punctuation to verify pronunciation and format respectively. Keep the Chinese field throughout processing so you can trace each result back to its source.

After copying, paste the result into an empty area of the target document and review the beginning and end. Verify tone marks in study notes and separators in table fields. If a character needs manual correction, review the syllable alongside the original sentence, then paste the corrected text into its final position.

  • Teaching materials or pronunciation notes. Use full pinyin with tone marks to verify how words and names are pronounced.
  • Lookup values or short labels. Verify separators, allowed letters, and duplicate names. Keep each value linked to its source text.
  • Mixed-text fields or file names. Paste the result into the destination and verify that commas, spaces, and line breaks meet its requirements.

faqs.q: Can I convert Chinese characters to pinyin initials only?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Output Mode, select Initials, choose a separator, and click Convert. For example, 「长大」 with Hyphen gives "z-d".

faqs.q: Why does ü remain after removing tone marks?
faqs.a: Full pinyin (no tones) removes tone marks and keeps ü. For example, 「女」 changes from "nǚ" to "nü".

faqs.q: How do I verify a character with multiple readings?
faqs.a: Convert the word that contains the character. For example, try 「银行」 and 「行走」 separately. If you are unsure how to pronounce a name, ask the person.
